false_passes_closed.found: The adversarial mutation suite MUTATED THE AUTHORITATIVE governance/project-state.json IN THE ACTIVE WORKING TREE and relied on a `finally` to restore it. That is safe only while exactly one runner exists and nothing ever interrupts it, and neither held during this round: a runner that outlived its wrapper kept mutating while a second run started, and each restored the bytes IT had captured, so the later restore silently reverted legitimate corrections. The canonical file was left with latest_transition_id=T0008 on one occasion and phases["1A"].status=NOT_STARTED plus an artifact-registry entry with its removal_gate blanked on another. The corruption did not look like a broken test; it looked like a broken repository.
false_passes_closed.why_it_passed: Nothing checked the harness itself. It was treated as a test rather than as adversarial software that writes to the one file the whole governance model depends on.
false_passes_closed.fix: The suite now runs every mutation in a DISPOSABLE SANDBOX: `git clone --shared --no-checkout` (objects borrowed through objects/info/alternates, so nothing can be written back and the sandbox has its own index, refs and config), plus a copy of every git-known working-tree file AND of ROOT/.git/index so the candidate's staged state is reproduced and not only its file contents. FIDELITY IS PROVED, NOT ASSUMED: the sandbox must match the checkout exactly on `git status --porcelain` (staged, unstaged, deleted, renamed and untracked-added) and on `git ls-files -s` (blob ids, stage numbers and MODES -- 100644 vs 100755, and 120000 for a symlink), or the run aborts. COVERAGE IS UNCHANGED because the sandbox is a real git repository, so the two git-dependent checks (SOURCE_COMMIT existence and manifest-vs-git equality) run exactly as they do in the checkout instead of being skipped. FAIL CLOSED: if the sandbox cannot be built or proved faithful the suite exits non-zero rather than falling back to the checkout. The suite also digests ROOT's governance/ before and after and reports ISOLATION VIOLATED if it ever differs.
false_passes_closed.termination_claims_stated_precisely: Normal exit, exception, SIGINT and SIGTERM are covered by finally + atexit + handlers. SIGKILL, and Windows TerminateProcess (which is what Popen.kill and Popen.terminate do there), run NO handler, so THIS PROCESS CANNOT PROMISE TO CLEAN UP AFTER A FORCED KILL and no such promise is made. What is guaranteed is the property that matters: the canonical checkout is untouched either way, because nothing is ever written to it. The leftover sandbox is collected by an INDEPENDENT mechanism -- every run sweeps psmut-* sandboxes older than two hours at startup, which is a different process doing the cleanup, the only kind of promise a killed process can keep.
false_passes_closed.case_limit_is_test_only: MUTATION_MAX_CASES exists so the isolation regression can launch short overlapping child runs. It is TEST-ONLY: the suite accepts --require-full and REFUSES TO RUN AT ALL (exit 2) while the variable is set, and it prints MUTATION_CASES_EXECUTED / MUTATION_CASES_TOTAL / MUTATION_CASE_LIMIT. The authoritative Project Governance step passes --require-full and then asserts from that output that the limit was 'none' and that executed == total, so a partial matrix cannot be mistaken for the full one.
false_passes_closed.proved: tools/tests/project_state_validator/run_isolation_regression.py, 13/13 PASS. A: three suites run CONCURRENTLY -- the exact shape that corrupted the tree -- all exit 0, each builds its own sandbox, and the canonical project-state.json digest and the full `git status --porcelain` are unchanged. B1: SIGTERM; checkout unchanged (on Windows the sandbox survived, and the test SAYS SO rather than claiming cleanup). B2: forced kill; checkout unchanged, sandbox survives exactly as documented. B3: a stale sandbox aged past the threshold is removed by the next run's startup sweep, which reports what it collected. C: with sandbox creation forced to fail the suite exits 2 with 'refusing to mutate the canonical checkout' and changes nothing. Every case asserts BOTH the project-state digest AND the whole working-tree status, because a suite that restored the file but left an unrelated path dirty would still have written to a tree somebody is working in.
